handbookNote: Alabama Real Estate Broker license exam. Genuinely NEW track -- Alabama previously had no broker-tier track on this site, only al_re_salesperson. Exam vendor: Pearson VUE, under contract with the Alabama Real Estate Commission (AREC). PRIMARY-CONFIRMED by directly downloading and reading Pearson VUE's own official Alabama Candidate Handbook (093300.pdf) and Content Outlines (093301.pdf, effective 2/1/2026). Exam mechanics: National/General portion 80 items (2.5 hours) + Alabama State portion 40 items (1 hour) = 120 items, 3.5 hours combined, $73 fee, 10-15 pretest items. Passing: a flat scaled score of 70 (0-100 scale), the SAME threshold for both salespersons and brokers. track_registry models this as exam_question_count=120, exam_duration_sec=12600, pass_percent=70, min_correct=84 (120 x 0.70 = 84 exactly). Broker eligibility: 60-clock-hour pre-license course (minimum grade 70) plus 24 of the preceding 36 months holding an active license in any state. CONTENT OUTLINE -- National/General portion, quoted from Pearson VUE's own outline (Broker column, 80 items across 8 sections, summing exactly): I. Real Property Characteristics, Legal Descriptions, and Property Use 10 items; II. Forms of Ownership, Transfer, and Recording of Title 8 items; III. Property Value and Appraisal 10 items; IV. Real Estate Contracts and Agency 15 items (largest national section); V. Real Estate Practice 12 items; VI. Property Disclosures and Environmental Issues 9 items; VII. Financing and Settlement 8 items; VIII. Real Estate Math Calculations 8 items. NOTABLE: this is Pearson VUE's OWN separate national template (8 sections/80 items) -- distinct from PSI's 11-section/75-item template used by every PSI-administered state in this campaign -- confirmed shared with wi_re_broker's own national outline structure (same 8 section names in the same order), meaning Pearson VUE and PSI each maintain their own single shared national template used consistently across every state they respectively administer. Alabama State portion (40 items, Broker column, effective 2/1/2026, summing exactly): Purpose of License Law/Rules/Role of Commission 0 items (Broker only -- Salesperson gets 1); Licensing Requirements 6; License Status 2; Broker Licenses, Company Licenses, and Place of Business 6; Recovery Fund 1; Disciplinary Actions and Process 3; Estimated Closing Statement 2; Trust Funds 3; RECAD (Real Estate Consumers Agency Disclosure Act) 5; Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions 12 (largest state section). This bank's bucket sizing is directly proportional to these real, Pearson-VUE-published item weights. Real Alabama statute/rule facts independently verified via the Alabama Real Estate Commission's own official site (arec.alabama.gov), whose 'License Law' section serves the full current text of Ala. Code Title 34, Chapter 27 and Alabama Administrative Code Chapter 790-X through an AJAX-loaded grid (GetLaws.aspx/ViewLaw.aspx) -- Justia, FindLaw, Casetext, and both the legacy and current Alabama Legislature sites were consistently blocked (Cloudflare challenges, DNS failures, or JS-only SPA shells) throughout this build, so AREC's own site (accessed via curl with a cookie jar to survive its ASP.NET redirect loop) became the primary working source for nearly every state-specific citation. Notable real Alabama citations used: Ala. Code Secs. 34-27-30, -32 through -36 (licensing, broker/company/branch structure, qualifying broker responsibilities, disciplinary sanctions and grounds), Sec. 34-27-31 (Recovery Fund -- $30 original-license fee contribution, $500,000 replenishment trigger, $50,000 per-licensee cap, $25,000 per-transaction cap, 12% statutory interest, all confirmed via live fetch), Secs. 34-27-80 through -88 (RECAD, Article 4 -- designated single agency, dual agency, and transaction-facilitator status; confirmed that 'subagency' is NOT a currently recognized RECAD category, correcting an initial draft error found and fixed during a dedicated re-verification pass), Alabama Administrative Code Rule 790-X-3-.03 (trust/escrow deposit timing, disbursement, and dispute procedures), Rule 790-X-3-.04 (Estimated Closing Statement -- required for single-family residential transactions, licensee must furnish and obtain a dated-signature acknowledgment), and Rule 790-X-2-.13/.15 (license status/reactivation). One topic (Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions) has a disclosed partial hedge: every question cites the real, confirmed Sec. 34-27-36(a) sanctions clause and, where relevant, Alabama Administrative Code ch. 790-X-3 at the chapter level, but the specific enumerated sub-paragraph number for each individual violation type (advertising vs. rebates vs. lotteries, etc.) could not be independently pinpoint-verified this session after repeated Cloudflare blocks on every remaining primary-source mirror -- flagged explicitly in-bank rather than guessed. Standard national real-estate/appraisal/finance/contract-law/math content not tied to an Alabama-specific statute is sourced to 'national real estate practice principles' framing throughout. Price set at $29.99 (2999 cents) to match this project's standardized Real Estate Broker track rate. This bank was drafted across 17 parallel single-topic drafting passes (8 national + 9 Alabama state-law categories, one-per-topic per this campaign's established model), each pass instructed to draft as many genuinely distinct, real, grounded questions as its topic's source material supports with NO target number or ceiling. Five state-portion topics (Licensing Requirements, License Status, Estimated Closing Statement, Trust Funds, Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions) initially stalled and produced zero output because too many concurrent agents doing live Alabama legal research fought over a single shared browser instance -- all five were relaunched individually with curl-first research instructions (browser tool as a capped last resort) and completed successfully; RECAD's original 7-question draft (also affected by the same contention, forced to use only a vague range citation) was separately re-verified live, which caught and fixed two genuine substantive errors (client-vs-customer duty allocation was backwards; 'subagency' was incorrectly presented as a valid RECAD category) in addition to sharpening all 7 citations to pinpoint subsections and adding 3 new questions. A cross-bucket source_note-citation dedup check across all 17 files found ZERO genuine cross-bucket near-duplicates. Answers were deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_al_re_broker_answers.js (global sequential-cycle rotation across all 17 bucket files combined, in file order), producing a final near-even 25.1/25.0/25.0/25.0% A/B/C/D distribution. 537 raw questions drafted against a 120-item exam -- a 4.47:1 pool ratio, clearing the standing 4:1 new-track floor, the final state of the N14 real-estate-broker campaign's 11th and last state.
